01-blog-sourdough.why: X has more voice but adds 'almost right away' and 'took a while'; Y keeps closer to the source though 'shows how far I've come' is stock.

02-blog-remote-work.why: Y's ending reads more natural, but it turns 'citing isolation' into 'because of isolation', stating the cited reason as fact.

03-blog-product-launch.why: Nearly identical; X's short prose reads a bit more like a person than Y's terse list.

04-email-deadline.why: Both are faithful; Y's subject line and 'before we meet' sound more natural.

05-email-followup.why: Both are faithful; X's 'Hi/Best' register fits a follow-up better than Y's leftover 'Dear/Warm regards' formality.

06-email-decline.why: Y is tighter and warmer; X keeps more of the stiff gratitude and confidence padding.

07-tech-readme.why: Both are faithful; Y's 'skips repeated work' and 'you are done' read more like a real README.

08-tech-postmortem.why: X adds 'We had no monitoring on the job' as fact and repeats the lesson; Y is leaner with a lighter inference.

09-tech-pr-description.why: Y adds an invented claim about how the vendor delivers events; X is a clean PR description.

10-essay-cities.why: Y has a stronger argumentative voice but inflates 'consequential' to 'done as much damage' and adds 'most people have never heard of them'.

11-essay-reading.why: Both are faithful; X's 'somehow hollow' sounds natural while Y's opening line is awkward.

12-essay-ai-art.why: X has more personal voice but invents 'more than anything else in my working life' and 'in the same week'.

13-slack-flaky-test.why: Both are faithful; Y's 'which fits the intermittent failures' re-explains what Aisha already said.

14-slack-meeting.why: Both are faithful and near-identical; Y's closing thanks fits a DM to a manager.

15-slack-review.why: Both are faithful; Y acknowledges Ken briefly and sounds like a person replying, while X is a bit blunt.
